source_documents.title: Aggregation‐Driven Thorough Cascaded Proton Transfer Process Targeting Ultralow‐Threshold Near‐Infrared Organic Single‐Crystal Lasers

reference_evidence_units.quote: the strong J-type coupling of 4260 cm−1 in DDMC single-crystal microwires effectively stabilizes TB* level by lowering excited state energy, supporting a thorough ESDPT process
reference_evidence_units.subject: DDMC
reference_evidence_units.statement: Strong J-type coupling in the crystal stabilises the double-proton-transfer tautomer TB*.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Coupling magnitude derived from spectra and calculation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: it is verified that J-aggregates in single crystal effectively lower the energy of TB*, enabling a thorough cascaded ESIPT process, whereas DDMC monomers undergo only a single incomplete ESIPT process
reference_evidence_units.subject: DDMC
reference_evidence_units.statement: Cascaded double ESIPT in J-aggregated crystals; single incomplete ESIPT in the monomer (PL, fluorescence upconversion, calculation).
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Lasing-oriented study; solution data are mainly spectral.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the second proton transfer is inferred to be feasible in aggregates but thermodynamically prohibited in monomer
reference_evidence_units.subject: DDMC
reference_evidence_units.statement: Calculated TB* lies above TA* in the monomer and below it in the aggregate.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground- and excited-state energies from DFT only.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Single ESIPT in the monomer and cascaded double ESIPT in the crystal are the paper's central mechanism.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: J-type exciton coupling in the crystal is what enables the second proton transfer; both are presented as the core explanation.
